question: As of October 2020 which of the following enterprises is NOT classified as a Maharatna company? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (11/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: NHPC
ONGC
BHEL
IOCL
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is NHPC

Explanation:
As of October 2020, the Government of India had granted Maharatna status to certain Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs), providing them with greater financial and administrative autonomy. The Maharatna companies included ONGC, IOCL, NTPC, SAIL, GAIL, Coal India, and BHEL. NHPC (National Hydroelectric Power Corporation) was not classified as a Maharatna company until October 2020; it was later granted Maharatna status in 2023. Therefore, among the given options, NHPC was not a Maharatna company.

question: The regulatory authority of money supply in India is the: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (11/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: SBI
RBI
SEBI
IRDA
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is RBI

Explanation:
The regulatory authority of money supply in India is the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). Established on April 1, 1935, the RBI acts as the central bank and manages monetary policy to control the supply of money in the economy using tools like CRR, SLR, and repo rate. Its primary objective is maintaining price stability while ensuring adequate credit flow. SBI is a commercial bank, SEBI regulates the capital market, and IRDA oversees the insurance sector.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Regulator of money supply → RBI
☛ Establishment of RBI → April 1, 1935
☛ Main objective of RBI → Price stability
☛ Monetary policy tools → CRR, SLR, repo rate
☛ SEBI regulates → Capital market
question_hi: भारत में मुद्रा आपूर्ति का नियामक प्राधिकरण कौन सा है? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (11/02/2021) Shift 2)

Explanation:

question: Which of the following is NOT considered as a pillar of human development? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (11/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: Equity
Empowerment
Justice
Sustainability
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Justice

Explanation:
The four main pillars of human development are Equity, Sustainability, Productivity, and Empowerment. These pillars form the foundation of the Human Development Index (HDI). Justice is not considered a pillar of human development; rather, it may be a goal or outcome of development. Equity means providing equal opportunities to all, empowerment means enhancing people's capabilities, and sustainability means development while conserving resources. Therefore, justice is not included among these four pillars.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Who releases the Human Development Index? → UNDP
☛ What is the main objective of human development? → Expanding people's capabilities
☛ What does the equity pillar mean? → Equal opportunities for all
☛ What does the sustainability pillar mean? → Conserving resources for future generations
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से किसे मानव विकास के स्तंभ के रूप में नहीं माना जाता है? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (11/02/2021) Shift 2)

सशक्तिकरण
न्याय
सततता

Solution: सही उत्तर है न्याय

Explanation:
मानव विकास के चार मुख्य स्तंभ हैं: समानता, सततता, उत्पादकता और सशक्तिकरण। ये स्तंभ मानव विकास सूचकांक (HDI) की नींव हैं। न्याय को मानव विकास के स्तंभ के रूप में शामिल नहीं किया जाता है, बल्कि यह विकास का एक लक्ष्य या परिणाम हो सकता है। समानता का अर्थ है सभी को समान अवसर प्रदान करना, सशक्तिकरण का अर्थ है लोगों की क्षमता बढ़ाना, और सततता का अर्थ है संसाधनों का संरक्षण करते हुए विकास करना। इसलिए, न्याय इन चार स्तंभों में शामिल नहीं है।

question: Jean Henry Dunant, a Swiss businessman, was the main inspiration for the setup of which international humanitarian organisation? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (12/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: International Committee of the Red Cross
World Food Programme
World Health Organisation
Global Forum for Disaster Reduction
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is International Committee of the Red Cross

Explanation:
Jean Henry Dunant, a Swiss businessman, was deeply moved by the suffering of thousands of wounded soldiers after the Battle of Solferino in 1859. He wrote a book, 'A Memory of Solferino', in 1862, proposing the creation of a neutral organization to help war casualties. His efforts led to the founding of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) in 1863. The ICRC provides humanitarian aid in armed conflicts and monitors compliance with the Geneva Conventions. Dunant was awarded the first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Who founded the Red Cross? → Jean Henry Dunant
☛ When was ICRC established? → 1863
☛ When did Dunant get the Nobel Peace Prize? → 1901
☛ When was the Battle of Solferino fought? → 1859
☛ What is the symbol of the Red Cross? → Red cross on white background
question_hi: स्विस व्यवसायी जीन हेनरी डुनैंट किस अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मानवीय संगठन की स्थापना के लिए मुख्य प्रेरणा थे? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (12/02/2021) Shift 1)

question: What does the term 'bank rate' refer to? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (12/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: Rate of interest charged by a central bank on its loans to a commercial bank
Rate of interest charged by a non-scheduled bank on its loans to individuals
Rate of interest charged by a scheduled commercial bank on its loans to a private sector bank
Rate of interest charged by a private sector bank on its loans to a commercial bank
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Rate of interest charged by a central bank on its loans to a commercial bank

Explanation:
The bank rate is the interest rate at which the central bank (e.g., RBI in India) provides long-term loans to commercial banks. It is a key monetary policy tool used to control the money supply in the economy. An increase in the bank rate makes borrowing costly for commercial banks, leading them to raise their interest rates, thereby reducing the money supply and helping control inflation. Conversely, a decrease in the bank rate makes borrowing cheaper, increasing the money supply. The bank rate differs from the repo rate, as the repo rate applies to short-term loans while the bank rate is for long-term loans.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What is bank rate? → The interest rate charged by central bank on long-term loans to commercial banks
☛ Who sets the bank rate in India? → Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
☛ Effect of increase in bank rate? → Decreases money supply and controls inflation
☛ Difference between bank rate and repo rate? → Bank rate for long-term loans, repo rate for short-term
☛ Which policy uses bank rate? → Monetary policy

question: Which of the following is NOT a function of Bureau of Indian Standards? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (12/02/2021) Shift 1)

question: Tools, machines, building, etc. that are required for production are called: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (08/03/2021) Shift 1)

question: Who is considered as the 'architect of Indian Planning'? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (19/03/2021) Shift 1)

Kshitish Chandra Neogy
Mokshagundam Visvesvaraya
solution:

Explanation:

Mahalanobis developed the 'Mahalanobis Model', a mathematical model used for resource allocation. He was also the founder of the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI). Due to his contributions, he was appointed as a advisor to the Planning Commission.

question: Under___________ economy, 'The decisions of what to produce, how much to produce and at what price to sell are taken by the market, by private enterprises, with the state having no economic role'. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (21/03/2021) Shift 1)
options: Capitalist
World
Mixed
State
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Capitalist

Explanation:
In a capitalist economy, the means of production are privately owned and economic decisions are determined by market forces. The state has no economic role; instead, prices are determined by demand and supply. This system encourages private enterprises to earn profit and promotes competition. In contrast, a mixed economy involves both government and private sector, while a state economy has the government making all decisions. The main objective of a capitalist economy is profit earning and it is based on the market mechanism. Capitalist economies are characterized by free markets, private property rights, and voluntary exchange. The absence of government intervention allows market forces to allocate resources efficiently. This system is also known as a free market or laissez-faire economy.

☛ Economy with no government intervention → Capitalist economy
☛ Feature of mixed economy → Participation of both government and private sector

☛ How prices are determined in capitalist economy → Based on demand and supply

question: Which of the following is INCORRECT about NNP (Net National Product)? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (21/03/2021) Shift 1)
options: NNP = GDP - Income from abroad - Depreciation
NNP = GNP - Depreciation
NNP divided by total population of a nation is equal to per capita income of that nation
NNP is the purest form of income of a nation
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is NNP = GDP - Income from abroad - Depreciation

Explanation:
The correct formula for NNP (Net National Product) is GNP - Depreciation. GNP includes income from abroad, while GDP does not. Option 1 incorrectly calculates NNP by subtracting income from abroad and depreciation from GDP. The correct formula is: NNP = GDP + Income from abroad - Depreciation. When NNP is divided by the total population, we get per capita income. NNP is considered the purest form of national income as it accounts for depreciation.

☛ Which is the purest form of national income? → NNP
question_hi: एनएनपी (नेट नेशनल प्रोडक्ट) के बारे में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन गलत है? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (21/03/2021) Shift 1)

एनएनपी किसी राष्ट्र की आय का सबसे शुद्ध रूप है।

question: In which year was Service Tax imposed in India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (21/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: 2002

1998
1995
solution:

Explanation:
Service Tax was first imposed in India in the year 1994. It was announced in the Union Budget 1994-95 presented by the then Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh. Initially, it was levied on only three services: telephone, insurance, and stock broking. The rate was set at 5%. Service Tax is an indirect tax collected by the service provider and deposited with the government. Until the introduction of GST in 2017, it remained a major source of revenue for the central government. After GST implementation, Service Tax was subsumed under Central GST (CGST) and State GST (SGST) for services.

Explanation:
भारत में सेवा कर को सबसे पहले 1994 में लागू किया गया था। यह तत्कालीन वित्त मंत्री मनमोहन सिंह द्वारा पेश किए गए बजट 1994-95 में घोषित किया गया था। प्रारंभ में सेवा कर केवल तीन सेवाओं पर लगाया गया था: टेलीफोन, बीमा, और स्टॉक ब्रोकिंग। इसकी दर 5% रखी गई थी। सेवा कर एक अप्रत्यक्ष कर है, जो सेवा प्रदाता द्वारा वसूला जाता है और सरकार को जमा किया जाता है। 2017 में जीएसटी लागू होने तक सेवा कर केंद्र सरकार का प्रमुख राजस्व स्रोत बना रहा। जीएसटी लागू होने के बाद सेवा कर का स्थान सेवाओं पर लगने वाले केंद्रीय जीएसटी (CGST) और राज्य जीएसटी (SGST) ने ले लिया।
